Reception is pretty good - can pick up several stations quite clearly, and a few more with some static. Sound quality is decent. You won't mistake it for CD-quality, but it's radio, after all. Battery life is very good - goes a few months on an AAA. I just switched to rechargeable batteries, but even with regular alkalines it's pretty cost effective.

The only downside I've encountered was the headphones. Found them to be very uncomfortable, and replaced them very soon after purchasing with a set of ear buds (not sure of the brand - perhaps Sony as well).

It's not as flexible as a MP3 player but I find the radio reception on this to be far better than the reception on my MP3 player that has an FM tuner. Yes, a conventional FM radio is a bit dated, but then again, so am I - sometimes it's nice to just listen to the radio. For the price, this is a great performer.

text_fidelity_a:
AKAMATE Active Noise Cancelling Headphones, Wireless Neckband Headset Bluetooth V4.2 in-Ear Waterproof Earbuds Magnetic Hi-Fi Stereo Sports Earphones with Mic, Carrying Bag There is always a run on headphones in our house. Not only are they being lost or dying, but everyone is on a constant quest for the best design and sound they can find in a bluetooth headphone. Let's see how these measure up.

WHAT ARE THESE HEADPHONES LIKE?
These headphones have a long sturdy neck band which means they will fit a variety of neck sizes. Each ear piece has a magnet on it so that when you are not using them, they will close in front of you so you won't lose them. The controls are at the end of the neck band on the right side.

ON/OFF BUTTON
Play, pause, on/off, pair can be done with this button.

VOLUME
The minus and plus of volume control is also used for skipping songs- + skip forward, - skip backward.

ANC
There is an ANC button on the right side directly behind the negative volume button which makes it easy to press them both at the same time. It does do noise canceling, but it is frustrating because it is easy to press the ANC button by mistake when also pressing the middle button.

CHARGING PORT
Charging port is on the edge of the control button area.

AI INDICATOR VOICE
The automatic voice is very dysfunctional. It only says part of words, and seems to be a bit mean sounding which makes my daughter say it feels creepy.

NOISE CANCELING
The noise canceling works beautifully on these headphones.

SOUND QUALITY
The sound quality is awesome. Highs and mids are where they should be. Bass is very good. It is not overdone but it is in balance and does not distract from the music. There are not any breakups in sound unless you walk away from the device.

BLUETOOTH RANGE
The bluetooth range seems to be good up to about 35 feet or so.

PHONE CALL QUALITY
The calls go through very well and people can hear just fine on phone calls.

BATTERY PERCENTAGE
There is no physical light indicator to tell you how much battery power you have left.

THE BOTTOM LINE
If you want a good solid set of headphones to use with phone and music that work well, are in balance, and great for listening. The controls are not as convenient as they could be, which can be frustrating at times.

MY RATING
Four stars. If the control area was set up just a little more conveniently so that you can not accidentally press the wrong buttons all of the time, they would probably be five stars.
text_fidelity_b: AKAMATE Active Noise Cancelling Headphones, Wireless Neckband Headset Bluetooth V4.2 in-Ear Waterproof Earbuds Magnetic Hi-Fi Stereo Sports Earphones with Mic, Carrying Bag

I have a 34” curved monitor plugged into the HDMI port, the refresh rate is 50Hz. Sometimes the external display is a little sluggish. On the plus side, I didn’t need any drivers. Plug and play.

The dock does not have an external power supply. It does support passthrough charging, it has a USB-C port for power in.

I like that the dock has three USB-A ports on the front. Much easier to plug in a flash drive or peripheral in the front of the dock rather than trying to see the back of it.

OTTERBOX SYMMETRY FOLIO SERIES Case for Microsoft Surface Pro 7 - Retail Packaging - STARRY NIGHT (CLEAR/BLACK/BLACK PU/DARK GREY MICROSUED) I ordered this OtterBox Symmetry Folio Series Case for use as my wife has a Surface Pro 7. The Pros and Cons are listed below:

Pros:
* The case fits the surface tablet quite snugly
* The back is clear, which allows you to showcase the Surface Pro 7's sleek encasement
* It has a fold-able cover that can be manipulated into a stand for the Surface when using it like a tablet
* The case's sides are made of a thick rubber that would provide some protection for the corners of your Surface
* The case base would provide decent protection

Con's:
* You can not use the case with the attachable Surface Keyboard, so you are limited in using your Surface only as a
tablet.
* The clear back scratches and marks easily. giving it a worn and unclear view of the back of your surface.
* The fold-able cover is not very good protection for your screen, it is relatively thin
* Because the cover is relatively thin, it is not really a stable stand when folded and the tablet is on it

This case does not really live up to the OtterBox brand. It seems quite an inconvenience to not be able to use your Surface keyboard without taking the case off. You would be limited in only being able to use your Surface as a Tablet. For some this maybe acceptable. But for my wife who travels extensively and uses her Surface more than her desktop for work, that just is not feasible. Plus, having to buy additional protection for your screen is also a negative aspect. I just would not trust this cover alone to keep the screen safe from breakage.

Overall, my wife will not be using this case on her Surface.
text_fidelity_b: OTTERBOX SYMMETRY FOLIO SERIES Case for Microsoft Surface Pro 7 - Retail Packaging - STARRY NIGHT (CLEAR/BLACK/BLACK PU/DARK GREY MICROSUED)

12x56 Monocular Telescope for Smartphone - Monoculars for Adults High Powered High Definition with Phone Adapter Tripod Clear Low Light Night Vision Telescopes for Hiking Hunting Bird Watching Camping The monocular works great, including in low light as advertised. It feels as solid as my name-brand binoculars, not like cheap plastic like some off-brands.

I’ve had binocular clips for phone cameras before this one, but this is the most sturdy design I’ve seen. I love it! I get very sick from shaking which meant for a long time monoculars were out of the question as well as some binoculars. It’s difficult to follow fast moving birds, but for ones that are sitting still this is an excellent option! I have a Pixel 6 Pro and had no problems hooking it up to the monoscope and giving it a whirl.

The tripod included is alright, it’s solid enough and when tightened well it works great, I found it a little fiddly to tighten and accidentally knocked off one of the knobs! It can hold the monoscope and my phone just fine despite the imbalance, and the universal mount means you can always use your tripod of choice.

We took some pictures from the cliffs near where we live, it’s pretty powerful. I also took a photo of the moon, you could see the pits and craters. It can be difficult to aim, especially at night but it seems to take practice–I didn’t use the tripod for that shot, which would have made it clearer. The woodchuck is with a tripod and fully zoomed.

What made me interested was the carrying case, which would fit perfectly into a hiking day-bag. My husband and I love to bird and this would be great for spotting owls at dusk! It’s stronger than my standard binoculars.
text_fidelity_b: 12x56 Monocular Telescope for Smartphone - Monoculars for Adults High Powered High Definition with Phone Adapter Tripod Clear Low Light Night Vision Telescopes for Hiking Hunting Bird Watching Camping

A tiny speaker the size of a soda can that creates a wonderful sound environment. I have it hooked to my Echo dot and the sound clarity is really good! And the bass coming out of the top is pretty precise. It's not the thundering bass but the correct one (to my ears). Takes up really a very small space.

Set up was very easy. Pressed a button to pair it with Echo using Bluetooth. My phone and Echo both picked it up really quick. Can't really tell if it's going to work in long distance but I have no reason to doubt what the manufacturer is claiming.

The only issue I had was figuring out how to use the volume buttons. I assume it's a quick press to lower or increase the volume but it's actually a long press. And then I am not sure how long to hold down the button to increase and decrease since there's no visual cue. But once I found the right volume it's OK. I can control the actual volume from the source as well.

I got the black one so it sits very nicely behind a few Knick Knacks and not really visible. The sound is "surround" so it's not directional. I have not paired it up with a twin to test out the stereo effect. But that's not how I intend to use this speaker anyways.

Very happy with this purchase. Kudos to the engineers for putting together such a nice speaker!

text_fidelity_a:
Kodak DC3400 2MP Digital Camera with 2x Optical Zoom I'm just an amateur when it comes to photography. All I really want is an easy-to-use point-and-shoot camera that I can take on vacations to snap shots of places I find interesting, to use around the house to take photos of valuables for insurance purposes, etc. In other words, my expectations are pretty minimal.
That said, I'm extremely happy with the Kodak DC3400. This is my second Kodak digital (my first was a DC240), so obviously I'm pleased with the Kodak product line.
After unpacking the DC3400, I spent about 10 minutes getting it set up, and proceeded to take a few pictures. Another 10 minutes or so, and I had the photo software loaded on my laptop. Connect the USB cable, and I was able to load the photos onto the laptop immediately. The camera shows up as an icon, like a disk drive, which you can double-click to open and transfer the pictures to a folder on your hard drive -- piece of cake!
The quality of the pictures is amazing. I use the Ofoto service, and had some prints of some of my digital photos sent to my mother. According to her, you could not tell the difference between the digital images and those taken with a 35mm film camera. The colors were vivid, the images sharp -- just what you'd expect from the Kodak name.
I'll agree with most everyone else and say that batteries might be the only downside to this camera. It's definitely worth the investment to get the Kodak NiMh rechargables and the charger. The ONLY time I use NiCads is when I'm my NiMh set is in the recharger, and I need to snap a few pictures.
For the money, I don't think you can top this camera in terms of features, quality, and ease of use.
text_fidelity_b: Kodak DC3400 2MP Digital Camera with 2x Optical Zoom

Foldable Bluetooth Keyboard, Geyes Folding Wireless Keyboard with Portable Pocket Size, Aluminum Alloy Housing, Carrying Pouch, for iPad, iPhone, and More Tablets, Laptops and Smartphones(Gold) This folding keyboard is a bit of a betwixt and between product, but if it is the sort of thing you think you might use, then it’s got a lot to like about it. If you have a tablet (and my experience is with iPads so keep that in mind), then their built in keyboard is a better choice for short work just because it’s larger and more natural to type. For longer work, the choice will be more individual in that some people hate writing for extended time on the hard surface of a tablet keyboard and others don’t mind at all. I can do a pretty long stint and for really long work, I’ll shift over to a Bluetooth keyboard, either Apple’s own or a smaller Logitech one that also acts as a cover. I’d prefer both of those to this because again, they are larger and so more comfortable.

When one considers the keyboard as a phone accessory, then things change a bit, and this become a much more viable choice. If I have to do any halfway extensive typing on a phone for work (something beyond texting, an email or two, etc., then this would definitely be my preference over the phone itself.

1) it takes up very little space (and comes with a nice little pouch). Tossing it into a backpack is nothing, but I could easily fit it into a coat pocket, a cargo pants-like pocket, keep it in my car console without it blocking much space. None of which would be true for my wireless Apple keyboard or even my slimmer Logitech one. The additional “bulk” is therefore relatively negligible.

2) the typing is quite nice on it. I was pleasantly surprised at the key travel, the ease, the tactile sense.

3) It’s definitely small and a little cramped, but not so I notice it unless I’m typing for a long time (half hour or more) and then I just need to take a few minutes break. The small size doesn’t come into play too often. I had to readjust to the apostrophe, and one has to hunt and seek a bit for less-used keys, but that’s easy enough and once you’ve been typing for a while it becomes just as second nature as normal typing does. And it’s much faster and much more comfortable than extensive phone typing

4) the stand is a nice little touch that works quite well, placing the phone at a usable and pleasant working angle and letting you sue it in both portrait and landscape mode.

5) I haven’t exhausted the battery so can’t speak to how long it will go, but it’s certainly lasted a good number of hours, more than I’d ever use it for (if I’m working that long I’m going to my laptop or tablet)

6). Build quality seems sufficient. I wouldn’t say it feels highly durable, but nor would I call it cheap feeling or overly flimsy. And when it’s folded I have no concerns about it breaking.

All in all this was actually quite the pleasant surprise and again, if you would ever find yourself needing to use your phone for that sort of mid-range work (more than you’d want to do on a phone keyboard but not so much you’re turning to a laptop) then I’d highly recommend it.
text_fidelity_b: Foldable Bluetooth Keyboard, Geyes Folding Wireless Keyboard with Portable Pocket Size, Aluminum Alloy Housing, Carrying Pouch, for iPad, iPhone, and More Tablets, Laptops and Smartphones(Gold)

text_fidelity_a:
Michael Kors Lexington 2 Smartwatch - Black Stainless Steel If you like fully featured smart watches, it is hard to find anything this watch can't do! It runs Google's Wear OS, which is their watch variation of Android, so Google users should feel right at home with it. It's got a Play Store for apps, a really fluid interface, and of course it integrates really well with an Android Smartphone. I've been told it doesn't play as nicely with iPhones, but a lot of the core features are standardized and cross platform so it can still function as a really nice watch and allow notifications and call support regardless of device.
My wife had a Fossil Wear OS watch previously, and the feature set is very similar except for one huge plus this has: A SPEAKER! Many of the third party entry level Wear OS watches have a microphone for digital assistant commands and voice-to-text typing, but lack a speaker for it to talk back. So you have to read your responses on the screen and you can't exactly take phone calls. But THIS ONE DOES! Thanks to the speaker, you can full on take calls like a modern day Dick Tracy. That's really useful and cool, especially if you put your phone down or have it in a pocket you don't want to pull it out of all the time.
But here's the big con:
BATTERY LIFE. While this is better than other wear OS watches I've tried, it seems like Wear OS is so feature-filled, they generally need to be charged as often as smartphones do. Battery obviously depends on usage, but average use seems to last about a day or two at a time. Heavy usage and you'll need to top it off every night at least. This isn't the fault of this watch, but rather Wear OS in general. Other smart watches such as the Samsungs and FitBits can go for days to nearly a week on a charge, which means you not only won't have to worry about charging it more than once or twice a week, but you also can do sleep tracking and just leave it on at night. That's something I'm trying to do in order to have healthier sleeping habits. Some devices such as the Mi Band and Amazefit can go for around 20 days on a charge! I was using a Mi Band 3 before trying this watch, and while it doesn't run apps or have a full color screen or take phone calls, I think I prefer having a watch that only needs to be charged about once a month, and can show me my sleeping data as well as pedometer and activity charts, all while alerting me to notifications. I feel like Wear OS has a ways to go before I'm ready to switch over full time. The good news is that devices ARE getting better, as this shows. If you love Wear OS and the smartest features available, this is a good option. But personally I think I'm going back to my "smartwatch lite" that has less bells and whistles but actually fits better functionally into my life.
I want to give this 3.5 stars, I feel like 3 is too low because it IS good for what it is, but I also don't like it enough to use it daily. So settling on 4.
text_fidelity_b: Michael Kors Lexington 2 Smartwatch - Black Stainless Steel

Blink Indoor Home Security Camera System with Motion Detection, HD Video, 2-Year Battery Life and Cloud Storage Included - 3 Camera Kit In terms of installation, it really doesn't get any easier: basically just plug in the control module and tap a couple buttons to register each camera and you're in business. Took me all of 5 minutes.

The cameras themselves aren't feature rich - you're not going to find tilt/swivel/zoom or even night vision. But you can't expect it from cameras that operate in 2 AA for up to 2 years! They do what they're designed to do: basic monitoring with motion detection in a completely wireless setup (you can literally place the cameras anywhere!). An LED light can illuminate any recording in darkness.

There's no monthly service fee either - but the recordings you can take are only up to a minute long and there's a limit on how many.

I love these cameras for their ease of setup and complete mobility. The only reason I'm not giving them 5 stars is the lack of an outdoor camera option and a little bit buggy iOS app.

Update (11/27/2017): a couple negatives to the cameras:
(1) while each camera comes with a wall mount, orienting it just right (in my case on a front porch so I could see who's at the door) isn't all that easy (just because the camera doesn't have an area in its view doesn't mean it won't detect motion slightly outside it!)
(2) the cameras have no speakers. I knew this when buying, of course, but competing cameras in same price range do.
(3) I just asked Blink whether there are any plans for Apple HomeKIt support - and there aren't :-( This is a big negative for me because I'm starting to do some home automation and since we're an Apple household, I want HomeKit. So I'm going to be looking for another set of cameras instead of expanding my Blink set :-(

ASUS Transformer Book T100HA-C4-GR 10.1-Inch 2 in 1 Touchscreen Laptop (Cherry Trail Quad-Core Z8500 Processor, 4GB RAM, 64GB Storage, Windows 10), Gray This is a tablet running a real operating system (Windows 10) hooked up to a small keyboard with a trackpad. And it's all right.

It's thicker and heavier but smaller than my 11 inch MacBook Air, which makes it more convenient in some respects and less convenient in others. The MacBook Air is a used 2012 model with a Core i5 and 4gb ram. It's snappy, but it didn't come with an SD slot, and used it cost about a hundred more than this. The quad core atom processor on the transformer book is pretty fast for a tablet, but it is definitely a lightweight compared to a core i5. Or even an i3.

My iPad Air runs iOS. Way less versatile than Windows 10 in terms of doing work-a-day things, having a browser respond the way you're used to having it respond, etc., but it's still pretty good. However, the keyboard experience is something of a pain, especially since there's no trackpad and you have to touch the tablet face to do the mouse-like things. And using the mail program is harder on the iPad than it is on a mac laptop or on the transformer book.

The transformer book is noticeably slower than either of the other devices, but I was able to do everything I set out to do on it. The Office apps are good and integrate seamlessly with the other Office installations on my other stuff. The screen is as nice as or nicer than my iPad Air. I had a MeMo for a year, and I loved the screen on that. This is very similar - excellent resolution, nice and bright, a bit wider aspect than what the iPad Air has.

The sound is about as good as one would expect. Which is to say, meh. But that's what headphones are for.

Cortano makes it easy to get set up. I asked it to find the apps I wanted. When I want something from the control panel, I ask for that. Since this is my first time with Windows 10, having the assistant helps a lot.

There do seem to be some battery issues. Charging takes a long time. There was an issue with the MeMos, as well, that I sort of resolved by fully cycling the battery a couple of times.

All things considered, I like this tablet/transformer book quite a bit. My only significant issue with it is weight. For my purposes, the ultralight notebook or the regular tablet will meet my needs on any given day. However, if you like your PC desktop and need, essentially, a shuttle craft, though. this is a pretty good compromise machine. It's a decent enough tablet. You can do business stuff, check email, surf the web, and watch movies. You won't be transcoding video or playing resource intense games, but this ultimately is a nice tablet with a keyboard. Not a desktop substitute. Maybe not even a laptop substitute, depending on your needs. But definitely a nice tablet.

UPDATE WITH USAGE ISSUES:

I was getting really annoyed with battery life/charging issues. My iPad Air will stand by for a couple of weeks, no problem, whereas this thing dies if I leave it off the charger a couple of days. It also needs its OEM charger if you intend to charge it within a few hours time, as opposed to overnight and then some. I was able to solve some of this by running task manager and disabling some of the high impact background apps (Microsoft OneDrive is a big offender). And, similar to my other Asus tablet, the battery charging problem seems to improve with conditioning. On the positive side, the more I use this, the better I like it.
text_fidelity_b: ASUS Transformer Book T100HA-C4-GR 10.1-Inch 2 in 1 Touchscreen Laptop (Cherry Trail Quad-Core Z8500 Processor, 4GB RAM, 64GB Storage, Windows 10), Gray

Uniden BCD536HP HomePatrol Series Digital Phase 2 Base/Mobile Scanner with HPDB and Wi-Fi & (BC23A) Bearcat 15-Watt Amplified External Communications Speaker This review is for the Uniden BCD436HP I see reviews here for other radios, so not to be confused.
I used Amazon Prime Now to get the radio to me, in less than 1 hour (about 45 minutes) the delivery person was knocking on my door with my new receiver, wow, I was highly impressed and I will always check to see if Prime Now is available for all my deliveries from now on.....
So, the radio....
This receiver has a 4 gig SD card preloaded with every known frequency with text for the entire US and Canada. They have software called Sentinel you install on your PC and this is your gateway to all updates and firmware and it can control your radios SD card any way you like. Sentinel has an extensive database of all frequencies and let me say this again, all frequencies have text description included which is the most highly advanced scanner database system I have ever seen and I have owned scanner receivers most of my adult life, (long time)..
This is a digital receiver using the latest technology available. It can monitor any analog or digital TX (with some exceptions, like encrypted signals) and gives you extensive control over what you're listening to. There are FCC laws regarding what is legal and not legal to monitor and Uniden has got us right up to the maximum legally allowed to be monitored by civilians. If you are law enforcement persons you will have much more powerful receivers available to you capable of Cell phone conversation monitoring etc., things no civilian should even be interested in.
There is another version of this Uniden radio, the BCD536 which is a tabletop version. If you have large powerful outdoor weatherproof antennas the BCD536 is a good option and it is completely transferable to vehicle dash mount and back from your work desk to your vehicle.
I like this handheld BCD436 best personally for my purposes.
This is basically a plug and play receiver. It comes with 3 2300 milliamp rechargeable batteries, load those, charge them or just leave radio plugged in, enter your zip and you're in. Well theoretically that's how it works, in the real world? No.
When you first receive the radio I would suggest positioning yourself in front of your PC. Have the paper manual, the radio, you and your PC right there in front of you. Get ready to read and learn your radios keyboard layout and what these great, well thought out keys can do for you. You will learn, trust me, you will quickly come to love this radio.
Some cons:
No wall charger adopter included. You can charge from your PC's USB ports but you will need a wall charger with USB port. Most of us have several of these around the house from old cell phones etc. They work fine.
This unit should come with a nice wall charger adopter. That's really the only con, not to bad really.
Antennas:
Your ability to scan and receive signals on any scanner is proportionate to your antennas. The more robust and correct (correct meaning size, materials used etc).. You will need some nice antennas for this nice radio to increase your scanning powers. Amazon has some nice antennas, scannermaster.com has some also. Your local radio shop retailer will have some also. The included rubber ducky antenna is garbage, toss it from across the room to your garbage can, see if you can make a rim shot. Like I said, I have been playing with scanners for many years so I have many antennas to pick from.
Verdict:
This is without a doubt, the most powerful handheld scanning receiver available from any manufacturer. It is the luxury sedan of the scanning receiver world. It is easy and robust. It is backed up by Uniden's Sentinel software which will future proof your radio for many years to come.
I give Uniden 5 stars for this winner.
I give Amazon 5 stars for Prime Now 1 hour shipping, also a winner.

Edit:
Okay some people are wondering what the best accessories are for this receiver.
Go to scannermaster.com and look for the Austin Condor All-Band Portable BNC Antenna and the SpectrumForce Desk Mount for One Portable Scanner.
The Condor all band antenna is unsurpassed.
The desktop stand holds your handheld at the perfect viewing angle, you can listen and see all text clearly right beside your computer.
See my photos. The photos ended up sideways.... trying to fix this..... Amazon, can you turn my photos upright?
text_fidelity_b: Uniden BCD536HP HomePatrol Series Digital Phase 2 Base/Mobile Scanner with HPDB and Wi-Fi & (BC23A) Bearcat 15-Watt Amplified External Communications Speaker

I bought the 43" QLED Q60B. Also bought the Samsung 9200S soundbar with wireless sub, and then bought their wireless rear speakers. That part is awesome, but will be a separate review.

1- Despite checking answers and even asking the Samsung Specialist about Hands Free Alexa (ie. don't press the MIC button), the 2022 version DOES NOT have this feature, which of course, after buying it, installing it 10ft up in the corner of the bedroom, and trying to make it work.... had to call Samsung directly to troubleshoot, who said it is not available after 2021. 2- Not-so-Smart. I have had a ROKU on all my other Samsung TVs because they were older. So I became accustomed to much more variety it seems. Other than the big ones, the variety is disappointing, even in the music section.

3- I do not buy a TV outright only to have the manufacturer decide what I CAN'T remove. The first damn option in your "customizing" short cut bar, is SAMSUNG'S forced-on-you advertising slot, that cannot be moved out of the or removed, and I have no interest in it! There are a few others that can't be dropped, but can be moved.

4- Despite trying to follow the trend to smaller remotes, they missed the mark. People want quick access to things. Mute should ALWAYS have it's own button, not remembering to press and hold a specific button to mute it. Your Settings access is NOT intuitive. I trying to make it easier, you somehow over-complicated it. Some items are ambiguous (maybe it's under this one?), and I find myself searching for things and when I finally find them, the controls are often limited.

It's 2022, I just bought a quality TV from a previously adored and promoted-by-me brand, and I'm super pissed. My buddy's LG is much better, and I'm now going to add a fricking Roku to a TV that is state of the art. And for a 43" I could have gotten an off-name brand with awesome pic and Roku built in, for half the price!!!! Lesson Learned!

Boo to Samsung on this. And don't send me to your useless Facebook help page when you already dropped the ball!

text_fidelity_a:
TP-Link AC1200 Reliable Dual Band WiFi Router (Archer C50) Update, Aug 2016: It's been 5 months since I installed this router and it has the distinction of never needing to be rebooted yet! That's a record for me, since some of my past routers needed a reboot every week or two (or even every day or two). I continue to be impressed with the rock-solid performance of this TP-LINK. It's not fancy and lacks some high-end features, but I'll take solid, dependable performance over flash any day.

Original review:
While this router won’t satisfy the needs of those who have complex networking requirements or those who like to tinker and tweak, it offers solid performance, AC speeds and good coverage at a very reasonable price point. If you’re looking to go to AC speed but don’t want all the bells and whistles, this offers a lot for the money.

The footprint is very small compared with other routers I have, which is a nice change. The overall build quality seems very good, and the two antennae are firmly attached (another problem I’ve had with lower-end routers). It has an off switch which is handy if you need to do a reboot. It runs warm but not hot.

Setup is very straightforward if you want to keep the default settings. Basically just plug it into a PC, access the router menu with your browser, set the network name and password, and you’re done. You can access more advanced features if needed, but for a basic setup the time required is less than 5 minutes.

Performance has been impressive. I also have AC routers from D-Link and Linksys that are far more costly than this, but this little guy holds his own when it comes to coverage and throughput. For example, I get Internet connection speeds of about 62mBps with my D-Link DIR-880L. This router, with the same PC and network card, gives me 50mBps. Wireless coverage is a little more spotty with this router on fringe areas (e.g., for a PC located a floor above and at the opposite end of the house from the router) but it still maintains a connection, albeit at lower speeds.

This does lack some features that could be helpful for some situations. It has a USB port, but only has one, and it’s a 2.0 USB port. It lacks a gigabit port as well. But again, for the price, it offers a lot of performance. So far I’ve had zero problems or glitches.

This router won’t excite a power user or satisfy complex networking requirements/demands, but for the basics, it gets the job done with solid speed and performance. Well worth considering if you’re looking for an inexpensive router.
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link AC1200 Reliable Dual Band WiFi Router (Archer C50)

14AWG conductors and ground mean you can get the maximum out of most household circuits (because most are 15 amp). I don't like any extension cords or strips less than that to avoid voltage drop, overloading, etc.

Crucial X6 4TB Portable SSD - Up to 800MB/s - PC and Mac - USB 3.2 USB-C External Solid State Drive - CT4000X6SSD9 Crucial is one of the first names that comes to mind when I have needed reliable RAM for my systems in the past. I have a Crucial 500MB SSD in one of my systems and it has served me well over the years so I was interested in this SSD as a back-up option for pictures and data. It has proven to be a fine solution for my needs.

Right up front – yes, it works with Linux right out of the box. I plugged it into my Peppermint Linux system and the kernel immediately recognized the drive and made it available. It was on me to mount the drive, but this was a simple matter and I was able to access the file system and see drive statistics. Obviously it works with Windows so I won’t go into that.

This is a physically small device, slightly less than half the size of a cell phone (iPhone 6s is what I used for comparison). It will easily fit inside the change pocket in my jeans and can tuck just about anywhere. This is a double-edged sword. On one hand it is convenient to have something this small and easy to store, but it is also easy to misplace or even lose. If this stays in your laptop bag or briefcase it should be secure, but if you are in a habit of keeping things in your pockets instead be cautious.

Transfer speeds are good. I have not done benchmarks on this drive but I copied thousands of pictures (average size about 8mb per file, some more and some less) and it was significantly faster than the USB drive I have been using for a while and faster than many of the thumb drives I have been using for backups. I have no complaints.

This is a small and fast drive that just works. It works with Linux which for me is important, and it is small enough to tuck in my camera bag for making backups in the field.
text_fidelity_b: Crucial X6 4TB Portable SSD - Up to 800MB/s - PC and Mac - USB 3.2 USB-C External Solid State Drive - CT4000X6SSD9

text_fidelity_a:
Sony HT-A5000 5.1.2ch Dolby Atmos Sound Bar Surround Sound Home Theater with DTS:X and 360 Spatial Sound Mapping, works with Alexa and Google Assistant,Black This arrived well packaged and without issues. I've tried out several major brand soundbars in recent years, and I've yet to find any that are as good as the Sonys, at least as a television speaker. I've already got an A7000 that I'm familiar with to compare this A5000 with. It's a step down in price and feature set, but there's more to the differences than that.

The A7000 has cloth speaker covers on top, while this A5000 has plastic. It's my impression that the sound is a bit better out of the cloth, since it provides less of a reflective barrier, but it's also hard to keep clean and safe. Being on top of the speaker facing up, it's right where something can get pur or dropped on it, or a cat walking across it. The hard plastic seems much more resilient. It's also hard to tell on the sound, because the A5000 has two fewer speakers.

The top of this speaker is a textured plastic, like a car's dashboard. Not super fancy, but resilient. The A7000 has very shiny black plastic, which looks very nice and is easy to clean, but also lacks resilience and shows dust more readily.

The remote is infrared, so you need to have line of sight to the speaker for it to work, but it's full featured, even having buttons to control optional additional speakers. which I really appreciate.

The instruction book is pretty good. Setup is easy, especially if you connect it to a television. It'll put the menus right up on the screen. It's really built to be a television speaker with bluetooth and other inputs so it can be used for other things as a secondary purpose.

I'm still trying to figure out what I can do with the Chromecast feature that seems to be present in the speaker, but not in the television. So far I haven't had much luck connecting with Chromecast.

I definitely like the A7000 better, but there's a solid price difference. I love having a second HDMI input, since the way they've got these things set up, it outputs to my Sony television rather than the other way around, so I need to plug in extra devices to the soundbar, not the television, which makes it a weird decision to put so many more ports on the television than the speaker.

Great speaker, but still plenty of things that could be improved in a future version, like more satellite speaker compatibility, some kind of port passthrough from television, chromecast video, etc.
text_fidelity_b: Sony HT-A5000 5.1.2ch Dolby Atmos Sound Bar Surround Sound Home Theater with DTS:X and 360 Spatial Sound Mapping, works with Alexa and Google Assistant,Black

Canon 2562A002 EF 28-135mm f/3.5-5.6 is USM Standard Zoom Lens for Canon SLR Cameras The Canon 28-135mm f/3.5-5.6 lens with Image Stabilization is a very capable, and more importantly, affordable lens,and is perfect for times when you just want to have one lens on the camera but you also want to have a lot of options with your focal range. While you get the benefits of a slight wide to telephoto range in one handy package, you do lose in light stops as you move through the focal range (the maximum aperture stops down as you move toward the telephoto end of the range). This is where the image stabilization comes in very handy, and allows you to keep hand shake at bay even when you have to compromise on shutter speed to get the correct exposure.

I've had no complaints about the optical quality, I think you'll be pleased with the shots you get from it - the lens may be cheap but don't confuse that with what the quality of image this lens can provide. Keep in mind on a camera with a cropped sensor (any Canon DSLR model other than the 5D and 1D models) the focal range is equivalent to @45-215mm - you lose a bit of the wide angle advantage, but you get more telephoto, so it depends which end of the focal range you value the most as to whether that is a disadvantage or not.

text_fidelity_a:
Facebook Portal Mini - Smart Video Calling 8” Touch Screen Display with Alexa - Black The Portal is sort of like an Echo Show but with different strengths and weaknesses. There is SO MUCH I could say about this device, some good and some bad, but I'll try to stick to the more important points here.
The killer feature, as you may know from their ads, as the way it can automatically zoom in/out and follow faces in a video call. So essentially, you can move around a room hands-free and it will find you and make sure you're in the shot. It's like having your own personal camera man on call.
In my experience with it so far, this worked fairly well. Moving left or right, the camera followed me. If more people enter the shot, it will zoom out to get them all in. It isn't without limitations however, and sometimes you'll move too far and it can't see you. Other times it got confused and lost me (if I move out of the frame and back in, that usually fixed it). For the most part, it worked as expected.
The sound is actually EXCELLENT considering this is the Mini edition. I was expecting the sound to be more like the Echo Dot, but this has a very large speaker on the rear which is able to drive very impressively deep bass without even approaching max volume. So that was a pleasant surprise.
While it has its own "Hey Portal" voice commands, it ALSO comes with Amazon Alexa built in. That's where it sort of starts acting like a Facebook-branded Echo Show, playing music, announcements, showing you answers to questions, turning on/off digital things, etc. All the things you want Alexa to do. However, I was sad to find that it isn't considered an Echo device for certain Alexa features, such as multi-room music groups, the Ring doorbell, and probably other Alexa Skills that aren't supported on non-Amazon hardware. So you can't really replace an Alexa Show with this if you need those features.
Now, some things that are better than the Echo Show: PRIVACY. I know, this is Facebook we're talking about, but I really like that they included a tab to disable the camera (by covering it up, not just turning it off), microphone, or both. It's like they realized that someone was going to complain they don't want Facebook recording them in their living room and thought ahead to add that. The Amazon devices with cameras don't have a dedicated cover built in. Then there's video calling to people OTHER THAN OWNERS OF ANOTHER DEVICE. The latest Show devices from Amazon have cameras too, but you can only call other Echo Shows or phones with the Alexa app running. The Portal can call Facebook and Whatsapp users, which means I can actually reach other people I'd want to chat with. This isn't a perfect implementation either, however... For Whatsapp, it essentially uses Whatsapp's web functionality behind the scenes to connect to your account. If you use Whatsapp web on your computer, it will log you out of the Portal and you'll need to log back in again after using it. This is an unnecessarily silly extra step. I use Whatsapp web a lot, so we ended up using my wife's Whatsapp account on the Portal to call our family and friends so we wouldn't have to keep logging out and in.
Then there's media like Youtube- much like the Amazon Echo devices, Google has decided not to allow an official Youtube app for the Portal either. However, there IS a browser, and you can go to Youtube on it. This makes for an awkward user interface (and not just because you can't control it with your voice), but once the video is up it works fine. It not only plays beautifully full screen, but you can even go back to the home screen and it will continue playing as a picture-in-picture overlay which can be moved around the screen by dragging. That's pretty neat. It's almost like they tried to support Youtube as much as possible without actually having an official interface to abide by Google's rules.
Other fun features include Facebook games like Draw Something, Chess, Super Baseball Batting Derby, etc, which you can play against other friends on Facebook or Portal devices. Then there's a bunch of photo effects which are really fun Snapchat-style filters that follow your face in augmented reality-style real time. These features can be used not only in the Photobooth app, but also on ANY call with the device. Then there's my favorite fun feature: Story Time! This feature is sort of like the snapchat photobooth AR-style effects mentioned above, however you read a story and it will animate effects over your face to illustrate as you go. This can be done on the Story Time app on the device locally or in a call to another person. My kids actually really LOVE that feature, and my 2 year old likes to read along with me when we do it. I'll admit they are very cute and sometimes I've laughed out loud when I didn't expect what happens next in the animation being done to me.

Honestly, as an Alexa alternative to an Echo Show, it is close but not quite a replacement. As a video chat device, it is better but only if your contacts are on Facebook or Whatsapp. And even then, Whatsapp is only good if you don't use Whatsapp Web. I'd consider it a 3 star device for those caveats, however the Story Time feature as well as the camera that follows you is really quite cool. Add that they considered your privacy with the flap cover and I have to give this at least 4 stars. It really has so much going for it, and I'm hoping they can iron out some of the software kinks to make it even better in the future.
text_fidelity_b: Facebook Portal Mini - Smart Video Calling 8” Touch Screen Display with Alexa - Black

CORSAIR Hydro Series H105 AIO Liquid CPU Cooler, 240mm Thick Radiator, Dual 120mm PWM Fans I've wanted to try one of these liquid CPU coolers for ages, but it always been a little too cheap to spend the extra money on one, and I confess I've been mildly concerned about using a liquid anything inside my computer. I'm glad I tried this out.

This particular model has a radiator style grate which the fan sits on (there is some conductive paste included), then has tubes leading to the cooler unit. The water is totally enclosed in the system, and I can see no danger of leakage. The fan is quiet and unobtrusive.

It has a four pin connector, so if your computer has a four pin connector as well, your computer can control the speed of the fan. However, the four pin connector can also connect to a three pin connector and it works fine, you just lose that extra bit of control.

The one small improvement I'd like to see is that the water/cooling area only goes to one side of the radiator type grate, not around all of the edges, so one side of it will always be hotter than the other. It still disperses heat well, just seems like a less efficient system then it could be.

Lastly, I love the thumbscrews included for installing. I hate dealing with normal screws, and the thumbscrews are such a thoughtful touch that it made me think well of the company for including them.

Overall, if you've been on the fence about testing out one of these new liquid CPU coolers, I don't see any reason not to try out this one. The price is reasonable for what it is, and it looks like a highly effective setup, certainly better than just using a fan.
text_fidelity_b: CORSAIR Hydro Series H105 AIO Liquid CPU Cooler, 240mm Thick Radiator, Dual 120mm PWM Fans

text_fidelity_a:
Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo, Full-Sized 2.4GHz Wireless Keyboard with Comfortable Palm Rest and Optical Wireless Mouse for Windows, Mac OS PC/Desktops/Computer/Laptops I've used much worse keyboards and mice, but I've also used much better. The keyboard is not bad, but speed typists would definitely prefer better. Because this is a full-size keyboard, be aware that you'll need ample space on your pull-out keyboard drawer. Some office desks have very narrow and shallow drawers. The mouse is okay too but feels a little cheap. However, this product was obviously not intended to be top-end.

My main criticism of this package is the somewhat confusing owner's manual. Every USB product I've used, particularly a kb or mouse, are plug-and-play. The manual gave instructions for "repairing' with the device, and it was unclear why you would need to issue the series of key commands in order to reconnect via USB on a PC. Perhaps this connection procedure applies only to other types of devices. After one brief failed attempt to connect (see next paragraph), the second try connected okay after I plugged in the USB dongle. I also unplugged/replugged the dongle and it worked again, without having to issue any of the "Esc + K" keypresses that the manual stated were necessary to repair the devices.

I suspect the range of this pairing is not very far. The first time I plugged the dongle in, neither the kb nor the mouse worked. I had to move both closer to the dongle before I got them to connect. The kb and mouse were only four feet from the dongle when I first installed them. After I finally got everything to connect at close range, I moved the kb and mouse back to the distance of four feet, and they continued to work. So I'm not sure of what distance would cause a disconnect.
text_fidelity_b: Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo, Full-Sized 2.4GHz Wireless Keyboard with Comfortable Palm Rest and Optical Wireless Mouse for Windows, Mac OS PC/Desktops/Computer/Laptops

text_fidelity_a: SkipDr DVD and CD Manual Disc Repair System, Single I was a little nervous about this product given the mixed reviews. It comes with the machine, a solution, and a rubbing cloth.  My daughters favorite Disney movie was scratched and skipping a lot so I wanted to fix it.  I wet the cd with the solution and placed it in the machine.  The machine has to be set on a hard flat service. I tried to just hold it in the air and it would not work. I made one round and then reapplied the solution, then cranked the machine around again.  (It goes slowly). I buffed the DVD with the cloth as directed and played the DVD. It skipped less than before, but was still skipping. Sangean WR-2 AM / FM-RBDS Wooden Cabinet Digital Tuning Radio (Black) First of all, my first order arrived with a small crack in the wooden cabinet and it would not turn on. I am going to give Sangean the benefit of the doubt and assume that it was shipping damage even though the box from the outside did not look like it was damaged, so I won't let this affect my rating.

But this did give me a chance to test Amazon's return policy, and I must say it was great. When I realized that I had to return the radio, I went to Amazon's website and clicked on the radio and selected "return." Then I was prompted to print a return shipping label to attach to the box when I sent it back. By the time I did that, there was an email in my in box from Amazon telling me that they were shipping a replacement to me via UPS Air. So I packed up the unit in it's original box, attached the label I had printed, and then the next day when the replacement arrived I gave the box to the UPS driver. Of course, all of this was at no additional cost to me. I was quite impressed with the whole process.

Now to the radio itself. Overall I am quite impressed with it and I am giving it four stars. For a radio of it's size, it sounds great. I have never heard a radio that small with the tight bass response that this one has. And AM radio sounds better than than it does even on my Onkyo receiver that I have in my family room.

The radio with it's wooden cabinet looks great on my nightstand and you can just tell by looking at it that it is a quality product.

The tuner's sensitivity on the FM band is good with the external wire antenna that is supplied with it. Selectivity between adjacent stations is also good. And I am getting good stereo separation when I listen with headphones. I do have one small quibble however. There is a button to switch any FM station to mono, but you have to do this individually for each station. It would have been better if you could toggle between stereo and mono for all the stations at once rather than having to do it individually for each one.

AM sensitivity is pretty good using the built in antenna. Weak stations in my area come in better than they did with my old clock radio, but I still do have some problems with the very weak stations. I could probably improve this if I bought a good external AM antenna, but I don't think I will bother to do that since I don't really listen to any of the weak stations anyway.

One reason why I got this radio was because it has a line in jack. I have connected my Directv box to it so that I can listen to the Directv music channels through the radio without having my TV set on. All I had to do was to go to Radio Shack and buy a Y adapter with two RCA plugs on one end and a 1/8" plug on the other. It works like a charm.

I also like that the display has large enough numerals that I can read it without my glasses on. However, as others have mentioned, the display defaults to the radio station frequency or the RDS display rather than to the time. To get the time display back I have to tap the display button, and it's hard to do at night in a dark room. I think it would have been better if it defaulted to the time in the first place.

Another quibble that I have is that the power button uses a bright blue light which is distracting in a dark room. They shouldn't have made it so bright. That will take some getting used to.

Also, as others have mentioned, setting the alarm is needlessly complicated as is turning it off. You need to hit three different buttons to do it. I am starting to get the hang of it, but I wish they would have just included a button which toggles the alarm on and off.

But overall I am rating this as a good four star product that could use some minor improvements. The most important thing to me is the sound quality, and that is unmatched for a radio of this size.
text_fidelity_b: Sangean WR-2 AM / FM-RBDS Wooden Cabinet Digital Tuning Radio (Black)

Setup of these speakers is straightforward and simple, so much so that instructions really are not needed to get started. The wire connector is color-coded to make connecting the speakers to each other almost completely foolproof. If I have any complaints about the setup it would be that the wire connector is a little on the short side but that’s an easy fix - just buy longer wire.

I enabled bluetooth on my tablet, told the speaker set to make itself available and the tablet connected to it immediately. One could not ask for anything simpler. The process took less than a minute and most of that time was spent walking across the room to press the bluetooth button on the speakers.

I loaded up Pandora and told the tablet to play and almost immediately it was clear that these speakers are far above average. The sound profile is stunning - clear and crisp highs, rich midrange and very satisfying bass without overdriving. These speakers do an outstanding job of accurately reproducing the sound. On the back of the main (control) speaker there are two knobs for adjusting the highs and lows should the middle be unsatisfactory for some reason. These speakers also do a good job with spacial elements and there is depth to the sound.

I paired the speakers with my laptop (once I powered off the tablet) as well and it was also very easy.

I took some cables and wired the speakers to an older television in the house to see how much better watching TV would be. It was definitely better and it have a more spacial and stereo sound experience but with our TV this prevented us from making any volume adjustments unless we turned the volume knob on the speaker itself. This is a minor nuisance but certainly not a real issue.

In addition to great sound, these seem to be well-build and rugged, a good sign right out of the box. These are an excellent choice for a home theater system or an audiophile's listening room.

So far I have found nothing about which to complain with these speakers. Set-up is a snap and the sound quality is just amazing. These are speakers for the serious listener.
text_fidelity_b: PreSonus C3.5 BT Channel Studio Monitor

Yooeur 12X50 Monocular Telescope-Compact Short-range Spotting Scope-Waterproof Fog Dust proof- Single Hand Focus My wife loves birdwatching and our teenage son enjoys stargazing so we have an assortment of binoculars and inexpensive telescopes. Before this monocular I had never used one and even though I have not had it very long at all I am already very pleased with it. Though it is ideal for bird watching and field work, it also will work as an amateur telescope.

At roughly 7" long, this monocular is large enough to be usable but small enough to fit in a coat pocket or even in a briefcase. It comes in a nice, nylon-weave carrying pouch that even has a belt loop so carrying it into the field is easy and does not take up extra room. It also has a holding strap much like a camcorder does so it can be held more securely. It has a small metal tripod suitable for setting up on a desk or table. It’s not a big tripod - the legs extend to 7.5" - but is works well if you are recording or are seated and need a steady hand. Finally, it includes a microfiber cleaning cloth in the box for wiping the lenses safely without scratching them.

This is a waterproof monocular and everything about it showcases that. There are two rubberized caps for either end that cover the lenses and keep out moisture and dust when not in use. These are physically attached to the barrel (one by a rubber flap and one by a nylon cord) so there is no issue with losing the caps. Most of the barrel is rubberized as well except for the focus knob assembly and where it attaches.

I used it to focus on the tree line behind the house (roughly 30 yards away) and was very pleased with how sharp and clear I was able to get the image. From the front of the house I was able to focus on the stop sign at the end of the street and had no issue with getting fine edge detail even at a distance of roughly a football field. The focus is very smooth and easy to adjust and getting the image in perfect focus is not the least bit difficult.

Though I enjoy cameras and optical equipment and I have learned a good bit about optical equipment I am a far cry from being an expert, so I took this monocular to work and approached two teammates who are very well-versed in optics, photography and astronomy and I asked them to look it over and give me their honest opinion. Both of them examined it and expressed their approval. They both said similar things about it: the image through this monocular is very bright and clear, the focus is very smooth and it seems to be very well made. They both made a comment about the lens and that it was very good due to not having a darkened coating.

One of my teammates told me to try looking at the stars with it. I had not really considered this but knew this would be an excellent test for it so I went outside after dark and pointed it skyward. Though I can definitely see more detail through a dedicated telescope, I was able to make out some of the larger surface detail on the moon including the high point in the middle of a crater. I was hindered by the fact that it is a full moon right now so I will have to try again this weekend during the eclipse. I then picked out a planet and looked at it through the monocular. Though it is a little tough to make out, I know I found Jupiter as I could see three of the moons as bright spots not visible to the naked eye (I have looked at it through a telescope so I recognize it from seeing it already). Finally I discovered a cluster of stars I could not see without magnification. This monocular is certainly not as good as a dedicated telescope but it is sufficient when camping and it eliminates the need to pack a big, bulky telescope unless you want to see more detail.

This is a great tool for use in the field. It has very good range, the image is bright and clear and it even is sufficient for stargazing should you choose to use it for everything on the road. Great product!

Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.
text_fidelity_b: Yooeur 12X50 Monocular Telescope-Compact Short-range Spotting Scope-Waterproof Fog Dust proof- Single Hand Focus

text_fidelity_a:
Creative Technology Speaker - for Portable use - USB This speaker set sounds great for its size. The sound is loud and clear, but also full in the way you would expect stereo sound to be. It is also small enough to travel fairly easily, although it is not the smallest on the market. This is capable of getting louder than you'll ever be able to use in a hotel room, but suitable for an apartment; there are plenty of options out there in the form of travel speakers.

The built in mic is obviously a significant factor, and it works great compared to my laptop mic. I do like the fact that it gets its power and signal over one cable, but sometimes I think I'm going to run out of USB ports since I use them regularly to charge my phones and other devices. And I was also expecting bluetooth after seeing the ads for the other models. But who cares about bluetooth when you still need power?-smaller speakers don't need an external power source.

This is a good product and I'm certain to use it, especially when travelling for long enough that I want to set up more of a "home" that includes music. It is sort of another take on what is already a niche product, however, and although I do think it's one of the better styles on the market, it's still not the end all of small speakers, nor does it make dramatic improvements over what is already available. It's great at packing full sound into something very portable, and it eliminates one cable if you use USB, but then you use up another USB port. I'd love to see it either fully wireless with included battery or also include a webcam to preclude the need for other accessories. Yes, I know these things would up the cost, but it would make a truly remarkable product.

I also like how the invisible button panel appears when powered on, but not how you can't completely turn it off without removing the power source. The speaker looks good and I like how all sides are covered in speaker screen material, but I worry I could easily stick my finger through a cone.

A quality product that is great if it closely fits your needs.
text_fidelity_b: Creative Technology Speaker - for Portable use - USB

NETGEAR WiFi Mesh Range Extender EX6400 - Coverage up to 2100 sq.ft. and 35 devices with AC1900 Dual Band Wireless Signal Booster & Repeater (up to 1900Mbps speed), plus Mesh Smart Roaming I have been using NETGEAR products for many years and am quite familiar with how they work and their quirks.

The fact that this unit has a built in Ethernet port is what led me to wanting this WiFi extender - the smart TV which is farthest from the primary router has had difficulty maintaining a solid connection so I wanted to utilize the Ethernet port on this extender to plug my TV directly into.

Set up of the extender was fairly straightforward, I plugged it into a power supply and ran an Ethernet cable from it to my laptop. The NETGEAR EXTENDER setup program auto loaded and was easy to follow. I setup the router to keep my same network name and password, it saved all of the information to my extender without issue. I unplugged the extender from both the power supply and my computer and located it into the bedroom, plugged it in and it found and connected to my WiFi without any issue. I plugged the smart TV into the Ethernet port and it connected beautifully - loading Netflix, HULU and Amazon Prime lightning fast.

The only hiccup happened when I finished that as the rest of my network went haywire with my smart devices not connecting and reconnecting. I restarted my modem and my primary router and everything appears to be back to operating as normal. I’m not sure what caused the glitch.

I can definitely see a WiFi speed increase in the area of the house that the extender is located and the TV that is plugged into the Ethernet port is streaming perfectly.

I am very pleased with this extender and would recommend it to anyone who needed to extend their WiFi range or provide an Ethernet Port to a device that is too far from their current hub.

Aibocn MFi Certified 30 Pin Sync and Charge Dock Cable (New Packaging × 2 Pack) This cable bears the MFi (Made for iPod/iPad/iPhone) logo on the packaging and looks nearly identical to the real thing. The only things different are there is no Apple logo on the cable and it does not carry the Apple price tag.

I tested it both as a charging cable and a synching cable with an iPad 2 and it performed flawlessly.

The thing that is the same is this is manufactured to Apple's specs and did earn the MFI certification. Why this is important to me is most third party manufacturers have dropped this legacy cable and are now licensing Apple's Lightning cable (if they are even MFi certified). Decent 30 pin cables are becoming scarce, and the ones from Apple are pricy. That leaves a lot of fly-by-night cables that have a high failure rate, and I am frankly tiring of replacing cables on a monthly basis (I had been purchasing them from a well known big box store as well as a nationwide electronics chain.) When I was offered this one as a review sample I could not resist.

I've been using this as my sole cable for over a week and am not disappointed. The construction is identical to Apple's, and the performance is too. If you are in the same quandary as I - experiencing high failure rates on 30 pin cables - check this one out.
text_fidelity_b: Aibocn MFi Certified 30 Pin Sync and Charge Dock Cable (New Packaging × 2 Pack)

1MORE Dual Driver BT ANC In-Ear Headphones Wireless Bluetooth Earphones with Active Noise Cancellation, ENC, Fast Charging, Magnetic Earbuds, Microphone and Volume Controls, Silver I returned these because of a software bug with ANC - and also because the call quality was terrible.

These phones stood out for being wireless with active noise cancellation (ANC) AND pass through (so you can hear ambient sounds for safety in the City). Unfortunately, those features are the weak points of the headphones - to the point that I found I would never use the pass through and often didn't bother with the ANC.

SOUND QUALITY: VERY GOOD - EXCEPT - they tend to exaggerate the mid base a little which can make vocals - especially male vocals sound a little unclear. Listening to the same music on speakers vs the headphones, it was just plane more real sounding and pleasant on good speakers. High standard, I know. Other headphones don't have that particular problem (though may have others - like weak bass or sibilant highs). I haven't heard that many competing models, so I don't know how they compare to sennheiser or bose or anyone else in the same price class. At least others have an app with equalization (Jabra, Jaybird).

Bug w. ANC: Sometimes it would say it's on when it's off and vice-versa.

ANNOYING THING: When you engage the pass-through, it has a voice prompt that tells you the pass through is engaged. Since often I switch on the pass through when it's important to hear something, the several seconds it takes to make its silly announcement means I miss part of what I was trying to hear! I found I would always just yank one plug out of my ear instead and get the instant feedback. ALSO - this thing takes FOREVER to turn off. You have to hold hold hold and finally it announces it's powering off. Combined with poor power indicator light - this is just annoying.

NOTE: This is not a defect, but just poor design... There is NO WAY to activate Google Assistant or Siri with These. Even my cheapo earbuds let you use one of the buttons to summon Google. Without that, how are you supposed to make voice calls? I have to pull out my phone to make calls. Foo.

Combined with atrocious call quality (I could hear them, but the person on the other end is always mishearing words or saying WHAT? WHAT?), these are DOA for me.

ONE LAST THING: The APP is garbage. Just pointless.
text_fidelity_b: 1MORE Dual Driver BT ANC In-Ear Headphones Wireless Bluetooth Earphones with Active Noise Cancellation, ENC, Fast Charging, Magnetic Earbuds, Microphone and Volume Controls, Silver

Linksys N300: Wi-Fi Wireless Router, Linksys Connect, Parental Controls, Home Internet, Wireless Devices up to 300 Mbps Transfer Speed (Black) I've been using a Linksys router for years and it never missed a beat (their wireless G model with the two antennas). But, after upgrading my Internet from DSL to cable, I thought a new router would be in order.

Before buying one I searched for reviews from computer and tech magazines/sites. Talk about confusing! I'd read one review that gave a sterling endorsement for a particular router; then another review from another site that gave the same router a horrible review.

Since my router needs are pretty basic (just use it to share Internet access) I concentrated on ease of install issues. In that regard there was consensus about how easy Linksys is to install. So I went with them again, and selected the 1200 model since it gave me all that I wanted/needed at a good price (but, to hedge my bets, I got it at a warehouse club so I could return it easily).

So happy with this router! Installation was SO simple -- if you can plug in a cable you can install this router. But, should you want to tinker with settings, you can also access the full, detailed configuration menu and tweak settings to your heart's content. I think it took me longer to open up the box and unwrap the router and power cord than it took to actually get it to work.

Performance so far has been excellent. I put it on the ground level of my house and have no problems getting a strong signal in the basement and upper level. I did find that it helps to put the router in the middle of the house rather than against a wall for best signal strength throughout the house.

Considering that my Linksys G is still cranking along after several years, I'm reasonably confident (or at least hopeful) that this will last me an equal length of time.

If you're looking for a solid, easy to install single band router, this is it. Highly recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Linksys N300: Wi-Fi Wireless Router, Linksys Connect, Parental Controls, Home Internet, Wireless Devices up to 300 Mbps Transfer Speed (Black)

The wireless charging works great for my Galaxy Note 8 (and does in fact Fast-Charge) however there have been a couple nights to where my phone was not charged the next morning. However for the wireless earbud charging, it does take some precise positioning to get them to charge. I noticed in other review that others weren't happy with the bright display light with no way to adjust it any dimmer than the lowest setting, however they must have updated that with a firmware update (which was super easy to do) as I had no issues with the display being too bright at night. I use the auto adjust setting which seems to work quite well as far as I can tell. Also I love the sleep mode sounds that you can adjust several (or just one) sound volumes to create your own personalized preference. I do wish that there were more sound options but the ones they provide are acceptable. I also wish that you could download and install more alarm sounds. Bluetooth connectivity is super quick and have never once had an issue with pairing it up to my phone. Really the ONLY issue I have with the Wakey is that to get the sleep mode sounds going, you need to connect with the app, and via Bluetooth connect to the device. No big deal right? Well my concern is that you will need to keep it connected for this feature to work. This means you will be connected to the Wakey ALL night and this kind of bugs me. It's just kind of creepy that the Wakey is connected to your phone all night while you sleep. I wish there was a way to just play your favorite white noise sleep sound by pressing a button on the Wakey device without having to always connect and stay connected to the app and your phone. The other gripe is that the plug design is huge and makes it so that I have had to move my nightstand further way from the wall to use it. Other than those two gripes, and the only reason for docking one star, the Soundcore Wakey is a very good product and a really great value.
*On a side note - I just tested the Wakey while watching some Youtube videos and the latency is not so good. There is quite a bit of delay and the voices do not sync up at all so I wouldn't recommend using the Wakey for listening to videos.
text_fidelity_b: Soundcore Wakey Bluetooth Speaker Powered by Anker with Alarm Clock, Stereo Sound, FM Radio, White Noise, QI Wireless Charger with 7.5W Charging for iPhone and 10W for Samsung

Webcam HD 1080p Web Camera, USB PC Computer Webcam with Microphone, Laptop Desktop Full HD Camera Video Webcam 110 Degree Widescreen, Pro Streaming Webcam for Recording, Calling, Conferencing, Gaming I've had this camera a few months. The install went pretty well. I had to reboot a few times to pick the camera up, but once it was recognized, that has worked well. The camera does not clamp securely onto my external monitor. I fixed that problem by getting a separate flexible arm that clamps onto my desk and holds the camara. I love the physical lens cover so I can easily control when the camera is capturing an image. The picture quality is great. I love having an external camera instead of relying on the one on my laptop so my laptop can stay connected to the docking station and I don't have to try to get it moved over to the center of my desk every time I have a videoconference. Unfortnately there there are two remaining problems that are making me now decide to look for another camera:

1. Echos: When using this camera, is it causes an echo on videoconferencing that others can hear. I cannot hear it. It is so annoying to others that immediately people start talking about it and asking if the call can be done using some other audio. It definitely happens on Microsoft Teams calls as others have said in the Questions section for this product on Amazon. I can't remember if it happened on Webex videocalls also. Others have said switching the audio source solves that problem.

2. Wide View: This may be standard on these cameras. I'll find out when I shop for a new one, but the view is much wider than my native laptop camera. I can't find any way on the camera to "crop" it so that it shows only the person during videoconference and not a lot of what is to the right and left of the person. I solved that problem by installing OBS Studio and the OBS virtual camera. OBS allows me to crop the picture and then uses that video as the "camera" in Microsoft Teams. That works very well to get a good cropped video, however, the image quality went way down and it freezes up sometimes, so it is not a great solution because I end up not having smooth starts to videoconferences with all the troubleshooting I have to do to get OBS, the webcam, and the conferecing software to all work together.

I hope I can find a camera that works seemlessly so that the now much more frequent videoconferences, thanks to the pandemic, will go more smoothly.
text_fidelity_b: Webcam HD 1080p Web Camera, USB PC Computer Webcam with Microphone, Laptop Desktop Full HD Camera Video Webcam 110 Degree Widescreen, Pro Streaming Webcam for Recording, Calling, Conferencing, Gaming

Also, even though my Wi-Fi router is upstairs on the other side of the house it’s picking up signal good and haven’t had an issue there.  This literally took like 30 minutes to install and get it running on my ring app.  I was pretty surprised.  I’m glad I bit the bullet and purchased this instead of a regular light.

text_fidelity_a:
ZOMEi Tripod, 65" Camera Tripod for Canon Nikon DSLR, Aluminum Alloy Tripod with 360 Degree Ball Head, Professional Tripod for Travel and Work (Orange) This tripod is advertised as 65 inches tall, but that is misleading since you can only reach that height with the center post full extended and somewhat unstable. Most tripods are measured with just the legs and not including the center post or head. This one is about 50 inches tall or 57 inches with the included ball head. You can compare that measurement to other brands.

For a tripod of this height, this one is relatively lightweight and folds up into a compact 20-inch-long case. That makes it very portable for field use. However, they did have to make a lot of compromises in stability to make it this compact and lightweight. The legs have 4 sections (compared to 2 or 3 sections on sturdier tripods) and the thinnest sections are somewhat flexy under moderate weight or in a moderate wind. I don't trust this tripod with a mid-weight SLR camera and exposures of more than 1 second (unless you have the legs folded to half length). For a lightweight camera and fast exposure, this tripod is fine. However, I still would not trust extending the center post in windy conditions, since that amplifies the instability of the tripod legs.

The tripod is attractively finished. I do not like all the twist locks that are slow to operate (compared to cam-locks) and with 4 leg sections, this tripod has lots of twist-locks.

The ball head works OK for this price level and has a quick release plate that also works OK. This company has several different quick release plates sold separately, hopefully one of those will work with this tripod so you can easily use different cameras on it. I have not tried to figure out which one to buy yet, though.

Other people are complaining about the zipper on the case. The zipper on my case broke on the first day of use, too. Just the zipper pull, which is not too expensive to replace.

In summary, this tripod works OK for this price level if you are using a smaller camera and fast exposures. If their goal was to make a lightweight portable tripod, I wish they had made it sturdier and shorter instead of flimsy and taller.
text_fidelity_b: ZOMEi Tripod, 65" Camera Tripod for Canon Nikon DSLR, Aluminum Alloy Tripod with 360 Degree Ball Head, Professional Tripod for Travel and Work (Orange)

Targus Demolition Backpack Designed to Fit up to 17.3-Inch Laptop, Black (TSB220US) Though I am giving a review for this backpack, I can't come from the perspective of having used it for a while. I only received my Targus backpack yesterday, but from the looks of it I am pretty darn sure this backpack will last a long, long time. I've used MANY backpacks in the past carrying books, laptops and supplies during the time it took to earn two separate college degrees, and at my previous job of 17 years. I had to carry tools, manuals, laptops and assorted parts to calibrate monitoring equipment around my state. I was rough on the backpacks and some wore out.

I really wish I had had a backpack like this one. It's very well constructed out of strong materials, has a plethora of pockets and places to organize your stuff, and though I don't have a 17" notebook as of yet, it appears to be deep and wide and should easily fit one. There are even slots for file folders and inside zipper pouches. There are pockets on the inside and pockets on the outside. The bottom inside has a foam rubber "shock pad" that neatly folds down flat on the bottom of the backpack and is about 1/2" thick. Plus the bottom is covered in a waterproof rubbery material that should definitely help keep water from seeping up into the bag. That happened to me several times on my job with my other backpacks and it was really frustrating. It's very easy to set your backpack down on the ground not realizing the area is wet.

The shoulder straps are padded and adjustable, and it has a waist strap for extra stability. Even if you didn't use this backpack to tote your 17" marvel of technology around, it would serve well as a camper/hiker backpack. I can't wait to start using it. If something should go wrong or tear up, I will most definitely update this review telling about it, but for now I can find no fault whatsoever with it.
text_fidelity_b: Targus Demolition Backpack Designed to Fit up to 17.3-Inch Laptop, Black (TSB220US)
