Jabra Evolve 75 UC Stereo Wireless Bluetooth Headset / Music Headphones Including Link 370 (U.S. Retail Packaging), Black Update:
After playing around and research I have found out that the bluetooth dongle is a separate device - called Jabra Link 370. With installation of the headset I also installed Jabra Direct suite. It apparently has Device Setting page, where one can choose between the dongle and the headset. The dongle settings have somewhat convoluted 'Wireless Range' option, which was - by default - set to VERY LOW (why?!) and after changing it to NORMAL, the signal seems to be much better and I experience no issues - so far... So, I'm boosting the score to 4 stars for now, penalizing Jabra with one star less to have set up VERY LOW as default settings (really?) and also not having any support on this issue. They had nothing about such transmission or poor signal quality issue in FAQs or their Support web pages - while the fix seems very, very simple and it should be there as one of the first FAQs.
-----------------
Original:
Got this set for about 2 weeks now in my open office space and the noise cancelling quality is amazing. Plus, great sound quality (I listen to a lot of music while working) until... it lasts... The sound drops out for a second to few seconds every 20-30 seconds, some sort of network overloading effect, humans sounding like robots, skips just like if you were getting our of range - while the dongle is about 2 feet from the headphones. This is the most irritating for music, but when it happens in the conference calls then it is no fun anymore...
The dongle is inserted in my docking station, but it doesn't matter, because I had the same issue when it was inserted directly into my Lenovo P50 ThinkPad. It also reproduces same errors when headset is connected directly to the laptop's Bluetooth, without the dongle.
For something that costs this much money, such flaw in the Bluetooth design is UNACCEPTABLE!

TP-Link Deco Whole Home Mesh WiFi System (Deco S4) – Up to 2,000 Sq.ft. Coverage, WiFi Router/Extender Replacement, Gigabit Ports, 1-Pack Been using for a few months now. Initially seemed like an excellent upgrade over an inexpensive single wifi router, but I've seen enough issues that I'm not sure I'd buy again. The worst failure was when I switched from Verizon Fios coax to ethernet and tried to use this as my main router. It worked... for about a week. At first, I just had trouble connecting to corp sites, so I thought it might be my corp network. Later that day, I saw issues with personal devices. Connecting to the router web page was super sluggish and the cpu was pegged. The next day, I went back to using the verizon router as the wired backbone and only using this set for wifi---much better. But, I still see occasional flakiness. Yesterday, one of the units wouldn't connect. I brought it closer to the other units---no dice. I rebooted. I connected it to the network via an ethernet cable. Finally, I rebooted the main/router unit and things went back to normal. Every 2-4 weeks one of the units has issues. Sometimes rebooting that unit is enough. Occasionally I have to reboot the main unit. One of the extender units connects via both wifi and powerline. The other extender unit only connects via powerline (it's too far to use wifi). The powerline-only unit is the one that tends to have issues. But, that was the point of buying this system.

So, the system seems good as long as you don't mind doing a ~weekly reboot. I see about 30Mbps over the powerline-only unit---not fast, but generally reliable.

I've started using MoCA (ethernet over coax) and will likely use that as my backbone in the near future---it's faster (I've seen ~300Mbps for a local transfer over MoCA/ethernet/wifi) and seems to be more reliable than this tp-link set over powerline.

Edit: I ditched this in favor of an EdgeRouter X and Ubiquity access points and am happier now. The Deco system was okay, but far from ideal.
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link Deco Whole Home Mesh WiFi System (Deco S4) – Up to 2,000 Sq.ft. Coverage, WiFi Router/Extender Replacement, Gigabit Ports, 1-Pack

text_fidelity_a:
Lexar E-Series 128GB Micro SD Card 2 Pack, microSDXC UHS-I Flash Memory Card with Adapter, 100MB/s, C10, U3, A1, V30, Full HD, 4K UHD, High Speed TF Card I've owned a few Lexar USB drives and Micro USB drives in the past and they have all had good quality and performance. I've attached the crystal diskmark performance below, but keep in mind that I am using the built-in microsd reader in my computer so speeds may vary as the reader has just as much to do with these benchmarks as the memory card itself.

I don't have any equipment that really stresses the microsd too much. The cameras that I have, while they can record up to 4K at 30fps, have generally had no problem writing to a U1 microsd. The Lexar, which I keep in my Osmo Pocket, is no exception, it has not had an issue recording video.

There is one key thing to point out about Lexar storage media that I've experienced in two of my past devices and that is the built-in expiration or time-bomb (if you don't agree with this philosophy). Lexar seems to have the philosophy that keeping your data intact is the most important when it comes to these products. Solid-state storage media has a theoretical limit to how many times they can be written to. Once that is hit, the media will be permanently damaged. Lexar has written into their firmware, a hard limit that once you write a certain number of times to their media, it will become read-only, keeping your data intact, but the storage unusable from that point on.

While I've experienced failed media in the past, I really only had this behavior with Lexar. I have to say, it did save my wife from losing the pictures on her phone if the card failed instead of becoming read-only.
text_fidelity_b: Lexar E-Series 128GB Micro SD Card 2 Pack, microSDXC UHS-I Flash Memory Card with Adapter, 100MB/s, C10, U3, A1, V30, Full HD, 4K UHD, High Speed TF Card

The headphones are small and just sit over the ears (like their noise canceling headphones). The Bluetooth component sits neatly inside the headphones, as we have another Bose Bluetooth headphones and the Bluetooth component sits outside of the headphones. I synced this with iPad, iPhone and iPod Classic (using Kokkia I10). The quality of the sound is fabulous as you would expect from BOSE ( a lot of bass) you will not be disappointed. The range is not miles...more like 20 feet..and not through too many walls. ...terrific design of compactness and total comfort on my ears. In terms of external noise, it really did cut out the concrete jungle living of traffic hum.

There are little and discreet volume up and down buttons, which are elevated a little so it is easy to find and you will not end up pushing the wrong button. I didn't have to press any additional button to synch..there is a voice telling you that it is seeking to synch..and will let you know when it has connected. The headphones remember all the names of the gadgets, and will play from which ever one that is 'on', which is a huge plus. There appears to be an intelligence here that we do not see in the Bose over the ear wireless headphones.

In term of play time, after a full charge, which took less than 2 hours: total playtime is more like 8 hours, not 15 hours claimed, but it must be related to the volume too. I had my volume pretty high most of the time. Given, how quickly it charged up, and the number of hours of playtime, I really don't need to charge it up for more than one every three days.

This product is so easy to install and works perfectly! The length of the cords is pretty much perfect, so I can station my two towers well away from each other and thus avoid heat buildup, which could happen if they had to be positioned too close to one another.

I would suggest only one or two small improvements to make this setup work even better. I would label the switch itself with A/B tags, and I would also put two, different colored LED lights on each end of the switcher, which would each light up, depending on which computer one is working on. That way, the user can quickly visually identify which computer is currently in use, instead of trying to guess.

I have put A/B tags on my switcher and on my respective computers too. However, since the switch is not a toggle switch, I often still have to figure out which computer I am working from when I don't remember where I left off the time before.

Otherwise, this device seems to perform seamlessly. Just remember that when you are rebooting one of the computers, be sure to keep the peripherals connected until they are recognized. Otherwise, when you toggle back again, you may find a screen with very large graphics on it - like I did once. I just had to reboot and stay with that computer until I saw the Windows welcome screen. After that all went fine.

I have a Windows 7 computer and an XP connected to this. My peripherals are HP w2007 Monitor, Altec Lansing VS2521 2.1 Powered Speaker System, Microsoft Natural Ergonomic Keyboard 4000 v1.0 (USB) and a Logitech Cordless Trackman Wheel (USB). Have not yet tried my Logitech USB Desktop Microphone.

Great product at a very nice price. I recommend it highly!

Pros:
The braided cable is a big plus for preventing flexing. The rubber collar at the connectors should prevent premature breakage. The length is a major advantage for charging ...(super advantage when traveling...think airports and hotel rooms)... and I am still able to perform both data and file transfers with a Galaxy S8+ without issue.

Cons: reason for downgrading from 5 stars... The Larger rectangular USB connector is loose in my Acer laptop ports with some wiggle that causes loss of connection. If you could scale tightness of fit on a scale of 1-10 I'd give these a "6". Fitment with my supplied Samsung charging block is nice and tight (a "10"). Also nice and tight . Several other USB cables and external devices I use with the same computer USB ports are tight and without problems... USB works fine but I have to check the connection to ensure contact.ection. text_fidelity_a:
Verbatim 128GB Ergo USB 3.0 Flash Drive – Blue I wasn't expecting this to be a speed demon, it says right on the box USB2 so I knew I wasn't going to get the 150+MB/s level speeds I get with some of my thumb drives. But even for USB2, this is on the slow side. Plugging in a standard sandisk drive to my USB2 port, I'm able to pull over 40MB/s without breaking a sweat. This one? Even on a USB3 port, I'm only able to pull a bit over 18MB/s in read, and the writing is even more abysmal. That's less than half of what USB2 can pull.
For the money, this is a decent delivery platform for you to hand off large files to someone, or perhaps to play media on a USB TV or something like that. But for regular daily transfer of data, you might find this painfully slow. As you can see in the benchmark screenshot attached, it timed out for the last two write tests and never even finished.
text_fidelity_b: Verbatim 128GB Ergo USB 3.0 Flash Drive – Blue

text_fidelity_a: ASUS C200 Chromebook 11.6 Inch (Intel Celeron, 2 GB, 16GB SSD, Black/Silver) I have an aging netbook that isn't really worth turning on anymore, and wanted a portable solution with a keyboard.  Unfortunately, the netbook market kinda died, but then again, the Chromebooks have seem to come into their own.  As a fan of ASUS's products, I couldn't turn this little guy down, especially at this price.  Over all, the build quality feels solid.  It's obviously plastic, but the construction is solid.  The screen on this Chromebook is serviceable, but has limited viewing angles.  Netflix and Amazon Prime videos seem to stream just fine.  The biggest surprise for me is the keyboard and touch pad.  Normally I have a hard time with touch pads, but this one is great!  And the keyboard feels like it belongs on a computer that cost 3 or 4 times as much (I own a $1000 ASUS gaming laptop.)  When it comes to performance, I do question how long this will last...  Scrolling though webpages isn't as smooth as it would be on a decent laptop, and I know that the guts of this machine aren't meant for high performance.  Regardless, this is definitely worth purchasing for convenience and portability!
